correctness.rationale: For any Noetherian integral domain A that is not a UFD, Hilbert basis theorem makes J=A[X] Noetherian, so ACCP and atomic. A has two nonassociate irreducible factorizations; in an integral-domain polynomial ring, factors of a nonzero constant have degree zero and units remain constant, so this obstruction persists in A[X]. The ordinary formal derivative D_X satisfies D_X(FG)=D_X(F)G+F D_X(G) with companion h=id completely multiplicative and D_X(X)=1, hence a nonzero L-additive function as defined in original Question 26. For A=Z[sqrt(-5)], norm a²+5b² has no values 2 or 3 and only unit norm 1; 6=2·3=(1+s)(1−s) is the explicit inequivalent irreducible factorization. Thus neither domain restriction, non-UFD property nor nonzero Leibniz derivative is extrapolated from bounded code; all have exact algebraic proofs.
